text:
Elaine (PM): Heads-up — Competitor 'LitePath' just announced a lower-cost routing tier. It limits per-tenant routing rules and removes advanced fallbacks. We should decide: ship parity (cheap, limited controls) or push our differentiators (per-route SLOs, fallback policies) and keep price premium.
Sofia (GTM): Seeing chatter in our outbound notes — several mid-market accounts asked for a cheaper option last quarter. Could be churn risk if we ignore.
Ana (Sales): +1 from customer signals. AcmePilot explicitly asked for a cheaper tier for their non-prod traffic. They said "we'd pay less if we can avoid advanced routing now." 
Matt (Eng): Quick feasibility: basic parity (drop advanced fallback + restrict per-tenant overrides) looks like ~2 sprints + 1 ops spike. Full parity with throughput tuning + new API hooks is 6+.
Ravi (Design): I can mock a simplified UX for a "Lite routing" flow in 3 days — no complex policy editor, just a toggle + dropdown for region.
Jordan (Data): Preliminary cost model: if we enable Lite, expected traffic mix shift could lower hosted rev but increase volume. Need break-even calc: price * usage elasticity. I can run sim with last 6 months data.
Elaine (PM): Proposed plan: 1) Quick parity experiment (Lite) as a controlled SKU for non-prod/low-SLO traffic. 2) Keep work on differentiator roadmap (per-route SLOs + intelligent fallback) but de-prioritize full parity until we see uptake. Thoughts?
Matt (Eng): Concern: parity path will complicate routing code and test matrix. If we ship quick, we must feature-flag heavily and keep default path unchanged.
Ravi (Design): Agree on feature-flagged UX. Also suggest a clear inline callout: "For production-critical workloads, use Advanced routing" — reduces misconfiguration risk.
Sofia (GTM): From GTM POV we need clear launch criteria and messaging. If Lite removes fallbacks we must call out degraded reliability guarantees. Want a 2-week beta with pilot clients (AcmePilot, BetaCo).
Ana (Sales): I can lock in AcmePilot and BetaCo for the 2-week beta — they'll give feedback and a small commit if it looks stable.
Jordan (Data): I'll produce the traffic sim and an expected revenue/ops cost delta by EOD Friday.
Matt (Eng): Acceptance criteria for the parity beta (draft):
```
- Feature-flagged Lite routing endpoint
- No advanced fallback enabled
- Beta only: allowed in non-prod tenants + opt-in for selected pilots
- Canary rollout: <=5% of traffic initially, automated rollback on error rate >0.5%
- Observability: per-route latency + cost metrics exposed
```
Ravi (Design): UX acceptance: onboarding banner, opt-in toggle, tooltip explaining tradeoffs.
Elaine (PM): Timeline suggestion: start spike this week (ops cost and testing), UI mock by mid-week, engineering spike -> beta in 2 sprints. Meanwhile continue gating full parity unless beta shows >30% conversion.
Matt (Eng): Will add feature-flag scaffolding. OpsBot — can you reserve a small dedicated capacity pool for the beta? 
OpsBot: Reserve request submitted — 2x small GPU nodes in staging for beta canary. ETA 4h.
Sofia (GTM): Messaging notes: highlight lower price, limited guarantees, and upgrade path to Advanced routing. Prep docs + pricing page copy during beta.
Ana (Sales): I'll prepare pilot acceptance questions to capture why they'd pick Lite vs keep Advanced. Good data for pricing decision.
Elaine (PM): Ok let's treat this as a reversible test. If Jordan's sim shows negative ROI or our error budget gets hit, we kill the experiment. Otherwise we consider a formal SKU and adjust roadmap. Thanks all — sync in #product-review on Friday for numbers.
